edits.issue: fact_103: 'can be exempted ... already states' does not match 'the Minister may exempt certain celebrants ... sufficiently states'. fact_100: wording paraphrased loosely ('any form recognised as sufficient by their religious body'). Neither is linked at the claim.
edits.fix: Under [section 46(2)](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/ma196185/s46.html), the Minister may exempt certain celebrants from section 46(1) where satisfied that their form of ceremony sufficiently states the nature and obligations of marriage. <!-- fact_103 --> Under [section 45(1)](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/ma196185/s45.html), when a minister of religion marries you, the marriage may be solemnised according to any form and ceremony recognised as sufficient for the purpose by the religious body or organisation of which they are a minister. <!-- fact_100 -->
edits.old: Some celebrants can be exempted from saying the section 46 words where their form of ceremony already states the nature and obligations of marriage. <!-- fact_103 --> When a minister of religion marries you, the ceremony may follow any form recognised as sufficient by their religious body. <!-- fact_100 -->
edits.new: Under [section 46(2)](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/ma196185/s46.html), the Minister may exempt certain celebrants from section 46(1) where satisfied that their form of ceremony sufficiently states the nature and obligations of marriage. <!-- fact_103 --> Under [section 45(1)](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/ma196185/s45.html), when a minister of religion marries you, the marriage may be solemnised according to any form and ceremony recognised as sufficient for the purpose by the religious body or organisation of which they are a minister. <!-- fact_100 -->

Talk to a lawyer to confirm your overseas marriage certificate is valid in Australia. <!-- fact_104 -->
